appraisal_events.evidence: In free indirect style from the worldly point of view: Robert «n'avait-il pas failli... se faire mettre au ban de son monde ? ne s'en était-il pas fallu de peu qu'il ne fût blackboulé au Jockey ? n'était-il pas un objet de risée par les folles dépenses qu'il faisait pour une femme de la dernière catégorie», set against an uncle who «avait su, non seulement garder, mais grandir encore sa situation de Guermantes... recherché, adulé par la société la plus choisie... aussi bon mari que bon fils !».
appraisal_events.explanation: The comparison condemns the nephew and crowns the uncle by the world's standard; the passage ironizes the verdict by opening on the law that the scolding uncle shares the nephew's faults and by letting the reader hold the secret of Charlus's «goûts véritables».

appraisal_events.evidence: He shrugs at what he takes for the narrator's naivety while «soutenir une erreur avec tant de certitude et de suffisance», praises brothels in terms that would have horrified him at Balbec, and offers to procure a «petite demoiselle de... d'Orgeville» or «la première femme de chambre de Mme Putbus» — unaware that the cheap house he despises is where «se donnait pour un louis cette Rachel que Robert avait tant aimée».
appraisal_events.explanation: Robert's own talk exposes him: complacently wrong about his uncle, coarsened out of his former severity, and blind to the irony the narrator silently withholds from him.

appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus, who «tenait impitoyablement à distance les maîtresses de son frère», goes to her «avec une amabilité dont la marquise fut d'autant plus agréablement surprise» that she expected coldness, and praises the Jacquet portrait with an enthusiasm Robert remarks on: «Regarde un peu l'empressement de mon oncle auprès de Mme de Surgis.»
appraisal_events.explanation: She receives conspicuous public deference from the family's usual gatekeeper against her; the narration undercuts the tribute by tracing it to her sons, whose charms he is really admiring in her face.

status_effects.explanation: The world's own reckoning is cited against him: nearly banned from his set, nearly blackballed at the Jockey, a standing joke for his expenditure on a woman of the lowest category.
In a separate moment of the passage the narrator's verdict falls on him directly: assured in error, complacent, and coarsened into a procurer's cynicism he once thought deserved death.
Even under ironic framing, the passage lets stand the social fact that he has enlarged his Guermantes position and is sought after and adulated by the most select society.
Witnessed deference where she expected a snub: the baron who freezes out his brother's mistresses courts her openly enough for Robert to point it out across the room.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly leaves Charlus's enthusiasm for Mme de Surgis undecided between calculation («pour l'accrocher») and sincerity («était peut-être aussi sincère»), which qualifies how far her elevation rests on a real tribute.
